recommendation: Keep the fix. It is a narrow active-source correction and should only be revisited if CQI later decides that evaluate reportType should deliberately support implementation-defined 'other' report types.
issue_request: FHIR-33004 is Applied/Persuasive and requested that the $evaluate-measure reportType parameter stop referring to the old subject/population values and be bound to a report type value set containing the evaluation report types individual, subject-list, and summary, excluding the data-collection/data-exchange report type.
initial_application: Commit 142c81d92f2c941402c0810650bf7b0e99edc6de for FHIR-28359 corrected the operation documentation from subject/population to individual/summary. Commit 287186099cc6119f4547894ca2e679b81fbda981 for FHIR-33004 created source/measure/valueset-measure-report-evaluation-type.xml and bound Measure/$evaluate-measure reportType to it. FHIR-37571 later copied that binding to the newer Measure/$evaluate operation.
additional_context: Measure is active in source/fhir.ini and source/measure/list-Measure-operations.xml includes both evaluate operations. FHIR-39174 was effectively treated as a duplicate of FHIR-33004 and cited the same implementation commit. Later FHIR-55083 added an 'other' escape-valve code to the shared MeasureReport Type code system without changing the evaluate operation definitions. Because the evaluation value set used include-all/exclude-data-exchange composition, it unintentionally began including 'other' even though the operation descriptions still list only individual, subject-list, and summary.
reconciliation: Changed source/measure/valueset-measure-report-evaluation-type.xml from including all MeasureReport Type codes except data-exchange to explicitly including individual, subject-list, and summary. This preserves the applied FHIR-33004/FHIR-39174 intent after the later shared-code-system expansion.
source_changes: source/measure/valueset-measure-report-evaluation-type.xml: replaced include-all/exclude-data-exchange composition with explicit individual, subject-list, and summary concepts.
